correctness.rationale: For every causal policy, the independence of the centered disturbance makes the first-state second moment equal its variance plus the first-control second moment. Strict positivity of the input diagonal weight forces budget equality. Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the only cross moment sharply and is attained by a homogeneous second-step gain, reducing the full causal policy class exactly to a strictly concave one-variable maximization on a compact interval. Completing the square produces an ellipse support whose constrained maximizer crosses zero initial excitation at the stated critical budget. The gain and optimal-value branches match continuously at that boundary. Separately derived dual curvatures prove the regular Riccati budget ceiling. The embedded standard-library verifier checks an exact witness in the quadratic field generated by the square root of three and 32,000 deterministic finite comparisons; the finite checks are corroborative, not the proof.

The present claim does not rename that mechanism: it analytically classifies all scalar two-observation instances with nonzero cross weight by a precise threshold, unique optimal initial second moment, frozen feedback gain, value branches, and exact feedback-only gap. value.rationale: The scalar two-step problem is the smallest horizon where initial control can shape later state-input information and a later feedback action can exploit it. It is therefore a naturally motivated complete classification of the regular-to-singular covariance-oracle boundary. Exact closed-form budget threshold, invariant post-threshold gain, unique optimal excitation energy, and strictly positive closed-form feedback-only gap clarify when the generic bisection family cannot spend the energy budget. These quantities can guide correct oracle implementation and demonstrate a real constrained-design distinction; the theorem claims no general higher-dimensional guarantee or algorithm-sized contribution.
